posts.author: JohnFP
posts.content_md:
Yellow has always captured my attention. Like how do you know if a yellow flower is reflecting yellow or green and red or some combination of yellow, green and red???

The problem you will have with using a yellow laser is it reflects it's peak at yellow. Now some green paints will look black to the pure yellow wavelength and some red paints will look black to the yellow paint. Furthermore, if the red paint reflected 20% yellow and the green paint reflected 20% yellow then both colors would look the same in the hologram. 

I will have to say sorry, but in my opinion it will not work as proposed. You may be able to control the yellow laser light to look green in the hologram with green paint and some shrinkage and the yellow laser to look yellow in the hologram with yellow paint but then again this is two processes disrouted and I doubt you will be able to extract red without further disjoining the processes. This would be even more complicated in finding the correct compliments of paints then the process I describe in doing my color DCG hologram.

But I like the thought, we need more thinking like this outside the box.

Peace

John

posts.content_md:
DJ, I dont see how a pure yellow wavelength reflecting off green, blue or red paint will record as anything other then yellow without shrinkage or swelling? Now if the yellow wavelength was that of a green laser and a red laser then yes, the red paint will reflect a lot of red and very little green and the green paint will reflect a lot of green an very little red and thus you would have two two separate wavelengths being recorded. But I just don't see how a pure yellow beam can be split by reflection off of paints into two primary colors red and green.

In your example, if you connect 570 (yellow, you made a mistake here) with let's say 470 (blue) you would get yellow, pale yellows, white and pale blues and blue. But I do not see getting green.

![ColorTriangle470and blue.JPG](https://holographyforum.org/forum/download/file.php?id=6226)

posts.author: JohnFP
posts.content_md:
Red and green laser = red, yellow and blue

Red and blue laser = red, purple and blue

Green and Blue laser = green, turquoise/pink and blue

Thus the best variety and more "independent colors" in my opinion would be the red and green lasers. Yellow seems to be the one color from the two primaries that is totally contrasty to those primaries to my vision then any two other primaries together. Purple looks like blue and turquoise looks like blue and pink looks like red. Nothing looks quite like yellow.

This is why I opted to expose in green and blue and swell to red and green.
